pages.text: Astronomy begins with gathering light. A $(item)Telescope Mirror Blank$() - glass, ground and silvered - collects a star's light over its whole face and brings it to one point. The wider the mirror, the fainter the stars it shows.

But no mirror focuses light to a true point. Light is a wave, and a round opening of diameter D spreads it into a disc about 1.22λ/D wide. Two stars closer than that blur into one: $(thing)the diffraction limit$(). Bigger mirrors are sharper as well as brighter.
